subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, make cron inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep cron limited to per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The choice creates a public config surface and defines the scheduled-run tool-execution security boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent precedence or compatibility behavior.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling cron and subagent semantics.

options.title: Keep current safeguards
options.body: Leave cron control to per-job `toolsAllow` and message-delivery safeguards, keeping config smaller but not solving the requested operator deny boundary.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review history and related security/product routing comments make `steipete` the strongest available owner for this boundary decision.
